qt: to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (ID) Subject:

The European Union aims to combat drug trafficking through the ‘European Ports Alliance’1. However, security management at ports is not the same in each country. There are difference, for example, between France, Belgium and the Netherlands. 1.

In this context, what specific measures does the Commission intend to put in place to ensure fair competition between the continent’s ports in the matter of security management, so as to take effective action against the surge in drugs coming into the EU?

What specific actions and technical means does it intend to use to promote cooperation between Member States in order to strengthen port surveillance, exchange of information and coordination among competent authorities with a view to effectively preventing criminal activities?

What role does it foresee for the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in this initiative, and how could the agency contribute to enhancing port security in a coordinated manner at European level?
at: (English version) to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (ID) (1 February 2024) Subject: Security management at European ports The European Union aims to combat drug trafficking through the ‘European Ports Alliance’ (1). However, security management at ports is not the same in each country. There are difference, for example, between France, Belgium and the Netherlands. 1. In this context, what specific measures does the Commission intend to put in place to ensure fair competition between the continent’s ports in the matter of security management, so as to take effective action against the surge in drugs coming into the EU? 2. What specific actions and technical means does it intend to use to promote cooperation between Member States in order to strengthen port surveillance, exchange of information and coordination among competent authorities with a view to effectively preventing criminal activities? 3. What role does it foresee for the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in this initiative, and how could the agency contribute to enhancing port security in a coordinated manner at European level? (5 April 2024) Raising the level-playing field of EU ports’ security starts with a clear assessment of gaps and weaknesses, while recognising ports’ crucial role in the EU’s economic prosperity. The Commission has conducted in 2023 a Schengen Thematic Evaluation on drug trafficking in ports. Complemented by an assessment of the customs activities on the ground together with Member States’ customs authorities, these findings and best practices will serve as a basis for the further development of the European Ports Alliance. As laid down in the EU Roadmap on the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime (2), the Commission will set up a framework to facilitate the effective risk management and customs controls linked to illicit drugs and drug precursors smuggling. From 2024, the Commission uses the Customs Control Equipment Instrument (CCEI) programme (3) to allocate over EUR 200 million to fund equipment that can help customs authorities scan containers and other means of transport. The Commission will also promote cooperation between customs and police within the European Multidisciplinary Platform Against Criminal Threats (EMPACT). In January 2024, the Commission launched the European Ports Alliance public private partnership (4), in order to promote best practices and put in place measures in cooperation with operators in and around the ports, as they use processes and equipment that could help identify insider threats in maritime supply chains. In this context, internationa l (5) and EU legislation (6) will be duly taken into consideration. In the context of fulfilling its primary task of border control at the external borders, the European Border and Coast Guard (Frontex) cooperates with the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) and the European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation (Eurojust) and provides support to Member States in the fight against cross-border crime.
